valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E per ADR (NYSE: RIO, USD), FY2027 EPS viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027). Share basis: 1 ADR = 1 ordinary share of Rio Tinto plc (ratio from general knowledge of the programme; not re-verified against the 20-F in this run). FX: none applied; Rio Tinto reports in US dollars so EPS is already USD. Base year: H1 2026 underlying EPS 421.4 US cents (vs 296.0 H1 2025), interim dividend US$2.11 (29 Jul 2026 results). FY2026 is estimated at about US$8.00 (H1 plus an assumed softer H2 of about US$3.80); FY2027 EPS is an operating assumption, not sourced consensus. Base: US$7.40 at 11x = 81.40. Bear: US$5.80 at 9x = 52.20. Bull: US$9.00 at 13x = 117.00. Price-only; dividends excluded.

bear.driver: Iron ore and copper prices fall back and cost inflation erodes margins; FY27 earnings about 27% below FY26 estimate

base.driver: Copper and aluminium strength partly offsets softer iron ore, earnings ease about 8% from FY26 estimate; cyclical multiple

bull.driver: Data-centre copper demand and firm iron ore lift earnings above FY26; market pays a higher multiple for copper growth

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS US$7.40 the 82.95 close implies 11.2x. The analyst targets seen (US$89.50 and US$90) imply about 12.1x to 12.2x base EPS, or EPS near US$8.10 at 11x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E on base EPS moves the base target by US$7.40 (about 8.9 pp of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Pilbara iron ore realised price and shipments, and copper output against guidance. A realised iron ore price well below the FY26 level would break the base case.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 operations review (January 2027) and the 2026 full-year results (about February 2027).

analyst_notes: Only a few dated named calls were found, all from a Google Finance listing summarised via search: Bernstein Buy with an US$89.50 target (9 Sep 2026), Morgan Stanley initiating at Sell with US$90 (21 Aug 2026), and an Erste Group downgrade to Hold (27 Aug 2026). The Morgan Stanley Sell with a target above the close is unusual and may reflect a listing quirk. Aggregator consensus ranges from about US$80 to US$107 and several are undated or stale; Argus Buy US$120 and Berenberg Hold US$87-88 (April) lacked exact dates and are not entered. Targets sit about 8-9% above the base case, a gap of roughly one P/E turn or US$0.70 of EPS.
